preamble: Affrication of the alveolar ejective fricative: [sʼ] is realized as the ejective affricate [tsʼ]. In Amharic the consonant written ጸ, with which ፀ has merged, is analysed as /sʼ/; Wikipedia, citing Hayward & Hayward (1999), says it can be heard as the fricative [sʼ] but is mostly heard as the affricate [tsʼ]. Wiktionary transcriptions show both: ጻፈ 'to write' and ፀሐይ 'sun' with t͡sʼ, ሕፃን 'baby' with sʼ. In Hausa the ejective sibilant written ts is [sʼ] or [tsʼ] depending on dialect (Newman 2014: 15). The sources consulted print Hausa words only with [sʼ] (Wiktionary's Kano transcriptions, Ladefoged's recording); the [tsʼ] side rests on Newman's transcription key and Wikipedia's general statements. They also disagree on which variety has which: Wiktionary gives Standard Kano Hausa [sʼ], while Wikipedia's article on ejectives calls [tsʼ] the standard form and [sʼ] dialectal. No source consulted gives a historical direction for either language. The Amharic /sʼ/ is a phonemic analysis, not a claim that the fricative is older (other atlas files treat Geʽez ጸ as [tsʼ]), and the Hausa pair is a dialect correspondence.

examples.note: ፀ continues Geʽez ḍ, which merged with ጸ. Wiktionary gives ሕፃን 'baby, infant' as /ˈhɨsʼan/, with the fricative.

examples.to: /(t)sʼún.(t)sʼúː/, with [tsʼ] in dialects that have the affricate
examples.note: Wiktionary. Newman (2014: 15): ts is "ejective [s’] or [ts’] depending on dialect". Ladefoged's recording likewise has the fricative in sʼaːràː 'arrange', contrasting with saːràː 'cut'.

sources: Newman, P. (2014). The Range and Beauty of Internal Reconstruction: Probing Hausa Linguistic History. Studies in African Languages and Cultures 48, 13–32. https://salc.uw.edu.pl/index.php/SALC/article/view/99

Ladefoged, P. (2006). A Course in Phonetics (5th ed.), web materials, chapter 6: Hausa ejectives and laryngealized consonants. UCLA. https://web.archive.org/web/20170113195516/http://www.phonetics.ucla.edu/course/chapter6/hausa/hausa.html
